answer: Each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squaring makes its challenge response depend on completion of the prior step, imposing sequential time that GPUs cannot remove for that instance. An attacker can run cloned identities in parallel only by allocating separate compute to each, so Sybil creation incurs real time and hardware cost rather than being free. Like a fable of a river split into channels, parallel effort does not shorten each channel’s path; a ripple of clones still faces the per-identity delay.
